newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian mobsters sentenced for journalist murder.
newsitem.headline: Italian mobsters sentenced for journalist murder.

text.p: A court sentenced six Naples gangsters to life terms on Monday for involvement in the killing in 1985 of an Italian journalist who probed organised crime in the southern city.

The six were Angelo Nuvoletta and Valentino Gionta, both bosses of the Camorra, or Naples mafia, accused of ordering Giancarlo Siani's killing, Luigi Baccante, Ciro Cappuccio, Ferdinando Cataldo and Armando Del Core.
Gabriele Donnarumma was sentenced to 28 years in prison and two other defendents were acquitted.
Siani, a reporter for the Naples daily Il Mattino, was shot dead in his car as he was driving home on September 23, 1985.
Investigators said at the time that they believed he was killed by the Camorra because of his investigative reports on the powerful crime organisation.
